lanes.lane: 3. codegen constrained by a component registry / design system
lanes.steal_what: Pinning the registry in the scaffold template itself (components.json + aliases) so constraint is a property of the project, not of the prompt.

One golden template + a prebuilt bootstrap snapshot for cold-start latency + the includeTemplate prompt toggle + declaring specific template files LOCKED so the agent extends rather than rewrites the scaffold.

Row security as a code-organization invariant: the model may only write handlers inside a blessed directory where identity is resolved by a platform helper, never raw queries — so the tenant filter cannot be forgotten.

lanes.lane: 7. deploy: hosted publish, wildcard subdomains, DNS/TLS
lanes.steal_what: deploy + addEnvironmentVariables as loop tools, and the 1/numDeploys scoring metric that penalises deploy-until-it-works instead of rewarding it.

lanes.steal_what: The 'what the platform handles for you (do not fight it)' prompt section — the single highest-leverage prompt idea for a scoped clone — plus the self-check loop (agent curls its own health_path before declaring done) and task_timeout as a DB column.

The idle-reap + wake-on-request lifecycle (the whole preview-cost model), per-sandbox-id locking around snapshot/restore/wake, and sandbox.yaml as the declared manifest (web.command, port, health_path) that a supervisor watches — a health_path contract is what makes 'is the preview up' answerable.

lanes.lane: 8. version history / rollback / checkpoints / git sync
lanes.steal_what: Host-side git push with the credential injected outside the sandbox (never exposed to generated code or the agent), snapshot rows scoped to the trusted tenant token rather than the untrusted user_id, and reserving visibility/format columns so sharing and compression are later slices with no migration.
Snapshot-as-template (any good build becomes a scaffold) and runtime preset as a DB row, so the template hub is data the platform curates rather than code it maintains.

The auth proxy pattern (agent gets a dummy key, platform injects the real one on the wire) — this single decision removes secret exfiltration from generated code as a threat; plus fail-closed egress and the boot-ordering rule that network rules are reconciled before the API accepts traffic.
Migration files that state their own invariants and reserve forward columns, with one runner owning the bookkeeping table.
